subject: Re: Order Form & DPA — 'shadow clause' on international flows
messages:
From: Emma Pryor <emma.pryor@clearwave.io>
To: tessa.morgan@redwood.ai, laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@clearwave.io, mark.douglass@clearwave.io
Date: 2027-11-30T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Draft DPA + Order Form redlines (high priority)

Tessa / Laura —

Thanks for the quick intake on this. Attached is our redline to the DPA and a separate EU dataflow diagram that highlights processing nodes outside the EEA. Our legal team flagged a clause in your current template (Section 7.4) that they say could permit what they described as a "shadow processing" scenario: vague subprocessor language + broad international fallback.

Key asks from our side:
- Confirm whether Redwood can commit to an EU-hosted inference path for all Clearwave customer data tied to this Order Form (orderable as a dedicated/private deployment).
- If not, provide a granular mapping of which subprocessors may access data and in which regions (we attached a first-pass diagram).
- Replace the broad fallback language in 7.4 with a transfer-impact addendum or explicit SCCs tie-out and a clear role map (processor/controller split).

We need a response by EOD Dec 2 so our procurement can keep the week-of-Dec 6 integration window.

Attachments: Clearwave_DPA_redline_v1.docx; EU-dataflow-diagram_v2.xlsx

Emma Pryor
General Counsel, Clearwave Systems
emma.pryor@clearwave.io

From: tessa.morgan@redwood.ai
To: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai
Cc: emma.pryor@clearwave.io
Date: 2027-11-30T11:04:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Draft DPA + Order Form redlines (high priority)

Laura / Ben —

Looping you both in. Emma flagged the term "shadow processing" which is our client's shorthand for ambiguous cross-border subprocessors + fallback operational routing. Clearwave is asking for a clean path: either a contractual guarantee (EU-only processing) or a detailed transfer-impact + SCCs solution with role allocation and KMS controls.

Proposed internal checklist before we respond: 
1) Legal: propose redline language to replace 7.4 with transfer-impact addendum text + SCCs reference.
2) Infra/SRE: confirm whether EU-dedicated inference can be guaranteed for the SKU in the Order Form or whether burst routes could send tokens to non-EU nodes.
3) Security: provide subprocessor list + KMS key custody options (customer-managed KMS?).
4) Commercial: note any pricing delta for locking to EU-dedicated vs. hosted fallback.

Emma wants an answer by EOD Dec 2 — two working days. I can coordinate a short external reply to set expectations; Laura/Ben, can you each flag the top 2 items you need to finalize language?

Thanks,
Tessa Morgan
Senior Solutions Manager, Redwood Inference
T: +1 (415) 555-0132

From: laura.bennett@redwood.ai
To: tessa.morgan@redwood.ai, emma.pryor@clearwave.io
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-11-30T13:27:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Draft DPA + Order Form redlines (high priority)

Tessa / Emma —

Thanks for the context, Emma — the materials are clear. I reviewed the redline and the problematic language in 7.4. My suggested approach: replace the single fallback sentence with a short Transfer Impact Addendum (TIA) clause that:

- Requires Redwood to use EU-hosted processing for "Customer Personal Data" unless Customer signs an explicit written exception.
- If fallback to non-EEA processing is required (e.g., DR or burst), Redwood will:
  * Provide SCCs as executed between the parties,
  * Publish a subprocessor access log for the affected request window, and
  * Offer a documented mitigation plan (encryption in transit + customer-managed KMS for persisted artifacts).

I will attach a redline snippet to the DPA that replaces 7.4 and add a short schedule defining roles (Controller = Clearwave; Processor = Redwood) with checkbox-style responsibilities.

Open questions for Redwood infra team (Ben):
- Can we guarantee processing locality for the SKU outlined in the Order Form if the customer commits to Redwood Dedicated or Redwood Private? If yes, specify the gating criteria (capacity reservation, burst allowances).
- Can we support customer-managed KMS for this deployment? If not, what is the alternative control?

I will produce a redline by EOD today and preface it with a short exec summary for Emma.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Privacy
Redwood Inference

From: ben.carter@redwood.ai
To: tessa.morgan@redwood.ai, laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: emma.pryor@clearwave.io, procurement@clearwave.io
Date: 2027-12-01T09:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Draft DPA + Order Form redlines (high priority)

Tessa / Laura / Emma —

Quick infra/procurement update:
- For the SKU under the Order Form, we can offer EU-only processing if Clearwave selects Redwood Dedicated (reserved capacity) or Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem). Our hosted multi-tenant plan currently routes by region but allows burst routing in constrained capacity windows — that is the root of the "shadow" concern.
- Pricing: EU-dedicated lock requires a 6-month minimum commit at +18% list rate. We should include both an upgrade path and a fallback SLO: if we cannot honor the EU-only path for a scheduled maintenance window, Redwood must provide advance notice + alternative processing certificate.
- KMS: customer-managed KMS is supported on Redwood Private; for Dedicated we offer HSM-backed keys managed by Redwood but can provide enterprise audit logs and envelope encryption.

Ben — happy to jump on a 20-min call with Clearwave to walk through capacity and pricing options.

Ben Carter
Head of Procurement, Redwood Inference

From: tessa.morgan@redwood.ai
To: Emma Pryor <emma.pryor@clearwave.io>, procurement@clearwave.io
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai, mark.douglass@clearwave.io
Date: 2027-12-02T15:04:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Order Form & DPA — 'shadow clause' on international flows

Emma / Mark —

Thanks for the redline and the diagram. Quick summary and next steps from Redwood:

Summary:
- We will replace the ambiguous 7.4 fallback language with a Transfer Impact Addendum (attached redline) and an SCCs tie-out schedule.
- We can guarantee EU-only processing only under Redwood Dedicated or Redwood Private (commit and pricing delta noted).
- For hosted customers (no dedicated commit) we will add explicit operational guardrails: documented subprocessor list, pre-notice for cross-border burst, and an emergency mitigation plan with encryption + logs.

Requested items from Clearwave to finalize the DPA:
1) Confirm whether you will order Redwood Dedicated or Redwood Private (this affects the contract language and KMS options).
2) If you require customer-managed KMS, confirm Private deployment so Laura can insert the relevant exhibit.
3) If you need SCCs executed before signature, confirm we should attach the combined SCCs file now (we attached SCCs-combined-clauses.pdf in our reply).

Next steps:
- Laura will send a clean redline to replace 7.4 and add the TIA schedule (before COB today).
- Ben will prepare a short commercial addendum with the Dedicated price delta and minimum term.
- Tessa will schedule a 20-minute call Wednesday Dec 8 to do a handoff demo of deployment options and review the EU-dataflow map.

I attached the draft redline and a copy of the SCCs we propose to use. Please confirm the deployment choice by EOD Dec 6 so we can align procurement and legal.

Thanks and talk soon,
Tessa Morgan
Senior Solutions Manager, Redwood Inference
Attachments: DPA_redline_TIA_snippet.docx; SCCs-combined-clauses.pdf
